business.title: Externally validated machine learning models for prediction of treatment selection and clinical outcomes in posterior communicating artery aneurysms
business.description: Posterior communicating artery (PCOM) aneurysms account for approximately 25% of intracranial aneurysms and present clinical challenges regarding optimal treatment selection. This study developed and validated machine learning models to predict treatment modality, complications, and functional outcomes in PCOM aneurysm management using a comprehensive institutional database of 75 patients treated between 2002 and 2023. Five machine learning algorithms—Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and XGBoost—were systematically compared across 7 outcome variables: treatment type (open vs. endovascular), specific open surgical treatment, specific endovascular treatment, intraoperative rupture, complications, angiographic obliteration, and discharge modified Rankin Scale score. Models were developed using preoperative patient-specific (age, sex, family history) and aneurysm-specific (size, presentation, morphology, location) parameters, with rigorous preprocessing that included class-balancing strategies, feature engineering, and regularization to minimize overfitting. Cross-validation performance demonstrated high accuracy for treatment prediction (78.7% Random Forest), complications (94.7% Random Forest; however, sensitivity of 0% indicates that this accuracy should not be interpreted as clinically useful event detection), intraoperative rupture (92.0% Random Forest), and angiographic obliteration (87.3% Random Forest). External validation on an independent cohort from the University of Louisville (n=20–28; n=20 most complete cases for the primary external cohort, with up to n=28 for selected endpoints with available labels) revealed variable generalizability: treatment prediction maintained 78.1% accuracy, and complication prediction showed reduced external performance (70.3%), highlighting institution-specific factors. Comprehensive sensitivity analyses demonstrated that class balancing significantly improved minority class recall (0.0% → 52.2%–86.3%) for rare outcomes. Feature importance analyses identified age, aneurysm size, admission modified Rankin Scale score, and Hunt-Hess grade as the most influential predictors across multiple outcomes. This study represents the first externally validated, multioutcome machine learning framework for PCOM aneurysm management, providing quantitative risk estimates and evidence-based decision support for treatment selection and outcome prediction.

science.title: Multistep synthesis of novel indole–benzimidazole hydrazone hybrids as xanthine oxidase inhibitors: In-Vitro evaluation, molecular docking, MD simulations and DFT studies
science.description: This work reports the synthesis of a focused library of indole-benzimidazole hydrazone hybrids (17-35) via a multistep procedure involving thiolation, hydrazination, and Schiff base condensation. The final structures were confirmed using 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and FT-IR spectroscopy by observing diagnostic NH, azomethine, and carbonyl peaks consistent with the proposed frameworks. All of the synthesized compounds were evaluated for in vitro xanthine oxidase (XO) inhibition, where only eight compounds possessed significant activity (IC₅₀ = 26.8–91.5 µM). Amongst the active molecules, compound 18 emerged as the most potent inhibitor (IC₅₀ ≈ 26–27 µM), followed by 20, 17, and 33, with several analogues outperforming allopurinol (IC₅₀ = 78.5 ± 1.34 µM), indicating promising lead potential. The structure-activity (SAR) analysis highlights that small, single electron-donating substituents at ortho/meta positions increased XO potency, whereas multiple, bulky, or strongly electron-withdrawing groups created steric clashes, hence reduced activity. Conceptual DFT results supported the biological trends, showing lower HOMO-LUMO gaps (3.75–4.37 eV) and reduced hardness relative to allopurinol, consistent with higher electronic softness and improved target interaction in active compounds. Molecular docking was performed against bovine XO (PDB: 3NRZ), which displayed strong binding of the active compounds (18, 20, 17, and 33) via cooperative H-bonding (Ser876), π–π stacking with phenylalanine residues, and π-cation/π-sulfur interactions (Lys771, Met770), rationalizing their inhibitory mechanisms. Furthermore, MD simulations were applied to compound 18, allopurinol as a standard, and APO, and the results reveal that after ligand binding, the protein was stabilized. The ligand-binding complex of compound 18 was found to be more stable than the allopurinol complex. The binding energy was calculated by MMPBSA; compound 18 has -28.839 ± 4.59 kcal/mol, and the allopurinol complex has -7.746 ± 2.53 kcal/mol. This interactive experimental-computational work identifies the indole-benzimidazole hydrazone scaffold, specifically compound 18, as a viable platform for producing next-generation XO inhibitors for the management of hyperuricemia and gout.

science.title: Glomalin-related soil protein and aggregate stability across a century-scale quercus liaotungensis restoration chronosequence on the loess plateau
science.description: Vegetation restoration can affect soil aggregate stability and organic carbon sequestration, but the role of glomalin-related soil protein (GRSP) within different aggregate fractions remains unclear, especially across century-scale restoration chronosequences. This study used a space-for-time chronosequence of Quercus liaotungensis forests (30, 60, 90, and 120 years) and abandoned farmland as the control (CK) on the Loess Plateau. Soil samples were collected at 0–20, 20–40, 40–60, and 60–80 cm depths. Wet sieving separated macroaggregates (> 250 μm), microaggregates (53–250 μm), and silt-clay particles (< 53 μm). Total GRSP (T-GRSP), easily extractable GRSP (EE-GRSP), and soil organic carbon (SOC) were measured in each fraction. Macroaggregate content and mean weight diameter (MWD) were generally higher in restored stands than in CK, with depth-specific peaks at intermediate restoration ages. SOC increased in all aggregate fractions after restoration relative to CK, especially in macroaggregates at 0–20 cm, and generally decreased with soil depth. T-GRSP generally accumulated with restoration age, whereas EE-GRSP showed a more pronounced peak at 60–90 years, particularly in macroaggregates. The EE-GRSP/T-GRSP ratio varied among fractions and depths and was highest at intermediate restoration stages. MWD was positively correlated with macroaggregate SOC at 0–20 cm and with macroaggregate EE-GRSP/T-GRSP at some deeper depths, but correlations were weak and based on a limited number of restoration-age groups. These results indicate that GRSP pools, especially in macroaggregates, are associated with aggregate stability during forest restoration, although causal relationships cannot be established from this observational chronosequence. The findings provide observational evidence for understanding soil structural recovery in semi-arid restored ecosystems, but broader extrapolation requires further validation across regions and soil types.
